subject: Private offers, reseller margin and marketplace packaging for CloudNova
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@cloudnova.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer + reseller margin questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo. CloudNova is interested in listing Redwood on both GCP and AWS marketplaces and we want to discuss private offers and reseller margins. A few items we need clarity on so we can take this to procurement: 

- Do you support private offers on both AWS and GCP (and if so, are the SKUs identical or separate)?
- What packaging options do you recommend for a reseller model (per-token, monthly reserved capacity, or instance-hour SKUs)?
- Target reseller margin: CloudNova usually needs 18–22% margin on marketplace transactions. Can Redwood support that band and what minimum ARR/commit is required?
- Pricing cadence: can we lock list price for 12 months in a private offer?

I've attached a brief requirements doc from our procurement team (CloudNova_Marketplace_Requirements.pdf). Marco from ResellCo (cc'd) will handle commercial ops.

Can you confirm next steps and a timeline for a private offer draft? Procurement is aiming to finalize by mid-June.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Partnerships
CloudNova Inc.

Attachments: CloudNova_Marketplace_Requirements.pdf

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer + reseller margin questions

Hi Elena — great to hear you want to move forward. Copying Ava (partner ops) and Sean (finance) so they can scope the private-offer flow and channel margin.

Quick answers up-front: we support private offers on AWS and GCP (Azure is possible but has a different flow). Packaging is flexible — we can create SKU families for reserved monthly capacity (committed vGPU-hours or token blocks) or token-based metered SKUs. Marketplaces require discrete SKUs per platform, but we can keep consistent pricing across them.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ava to propose packaging options and recommended channel margin bands.
2) Sean to provide commercial baseline (list price, Redwood discount to reseller, and sample margin math).
3) We exchange a draft private offer for CloudNova and ResellCo for review (DocuSign for signatures).

Can you confirm whether CloudNova prefers a 12-month committed SKU or metered monthly billing? Also confirm minimum ARR expectations (so we can evaluate margin flexibility).

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marco Diaz <m.diaz@resellco.io>
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer + reseller margin questions

Hi all — taking point on marketplace ops. Notes below based on recent AWS/GCP experience and the attachment you sent.

1) Platform support and SKUs- AWS and GCP both support private/offers but each requires a separate private-offer flow and separate SKU definitions. We should create parallel SKU families so billing and reporting line up across platforms.

2) Recommended packaging (pros/cons)- Monthly reserved capacity SKU (recommended): creates predictable ARR, simple billing for procurement. SKU example: "Redwood Dedicated - 1k token blocks / month" or "Redwood Reserved - 250 vGPU-hours / month".- Metered per-token SKU: flexible for smaller pilots but harder for procurement to forecast; higher operation overhead on CSV reconciliation.
- Hybrid: a committed monthly base + overage per-token (good for larger customers).

3) Channel margin guidance- Standard partner margin we approve for marketplaces: 12–15% at list price.
- For 12-month committed ARR above $120k/year we can stretch to 18–20% (requires finance sign-off and a modest promotional discount from Redwood).

4) Commercial constraints- Marketplaces enforce list prices and then private offer discounts are applied. Resellers see the marketplace price; the margin calculus depends on whether Redwood absorbs promotional credit or the reseller does.

I've attached a proposed pricing table that maps list SKUs, Redwood internal list, suggested marketplace price, and two margin scenarios (15% standard, 18% partner uplift) — see Proposed_Pricing_Table.xlsx.

I'll kick off the private-offer request for AWS and GCP once Sean confirms the numbers and we have CloudNova's preferred packaging (12-month commit vs metered).

Cheers,
Ava Chen
Partner Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Proposed_Pricing_Table.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Marco Diaz <m.diaz@resellco.io>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer + reseller margin questions (pricing math)

Thanks — crunched numbers and here's a workable approach. High level: we will offer a private-offer discount upfront to enable reseller margin while keeping Redwood unit economics intact.

Assumptions
- List price (public SKU): $0.50 per 1k tokens equivalent (example SKU).
- Redwood internal list (cost-to-serve estimate incl infra & ops): $0.25 per 1k tokens.

Scenario A: 15% reseller margin (standard)
- Marketplace price = $0.50
- Reseller sells at marketplace price, pocketing 15% margin = $0.075 per 1k tokens
- Redwood receives marketplace settlement = $0.425 per 1k tokens
- Gross to Redwood over cost = $0.175 per 1k tokens

Scenario B: 18% reseller margin with 12-month $150k ARR commit (stretch case)
- We will provide a 10% private-offer discount to the marketplace price to enable the margin and promotional credit (applied as part of private offer).
- Effective marketplace price seen by buyer = $0.45 per 1k tokens
- Reseller margin (18%) = $0.081 per 1k tokens
- Redwood net = ~$0.369 per 1k tokens
- Gross over cost = ~$0.119 per 1k tokens (acceptable given the ARR guarantee and minimum term)

Operational notes
- For AWS private offers we need a partner account and procurement contact; CloudNova's procurement team will accept the DocuSign + AWS private-offer ID.
- For GCP marketplace private offers, processing takes ~7–10 business days after we submit SKU definitions and pricing.

If that math looks OK, I'll prepare the DocuSign and the redlined private-offer terms (term length 12 months, early termination clause, SLAs). Placeholder DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/signer/abc123

Sean Gallagher
Senior Finance Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — helpful breakdown. CloudNova is prepared to proceed on the stretch case (18% reseller margin) under these conditions:

- 12-month committed SKU at $150k ARR (as Sean modeled)
- Redwood provides a one-time 10% promotional credit to be applied in the first invoice period
- 30-day SLA credit clause for resolved incidents impacting production availability
- Private-offer SKUs for AWS and GCP deployed in parallel; we will route procurement on our end once the private-offer drafts are ready.

Please proceed with the AWS and GCP private-offer submission and send DocuSign for signature. Procurement timeline: they expect to start internal review this week and aim to sign within three weeks.

Elena Rossi

CloudNova Inc.
